spans.s:
Nivānya-vatsā and Nivānyā in the Śatapatha brāhmaṇa denotes a ‘cow with a calf to which she has to be won over,’ that is, with a calf substituted for one of her own which has died. Nivānyā is a contracted form of the compound term. Similar expressions are abhivānya-vatsā, abhivānyā, vānyā, and apivānya-vatsā.
Foot notes xii. 5, 1, 4.
ii. 6, 1, 6.
aitareya brāhmaṇa, vii. 2.
taittirīya brāhmaṇa, i. 6, 8, 4.
Ibid., ii. 6, 16, 2.
kauśika sūtra, lxxxii. 22.
Cf. Lanman in Whitney's Translation of the Atharvaveda, 880.

Nivid-dhāna, ‘containing a nivid,’ is found several times as an epithet of a hymn or verse in the Brāhmaṇas.
Foot notes aitareya brāhmaṇa, iii. 17; Kauṣīaki brāhmaṇa, xxi. 6; xxiv. 4; Śatapatha brāhmaṇa, xiii. 5, 1, 12; aitareya Āraṇyaka, i. 2, 2; 5, 3.

Nīvāra, ‘wild rice,’ is mentioned in the yajurveda Saṃhitās and the Brāhmaṇas.
Foot notes kāṭhaka Saṃhitā, xii. 4; Maitrāyaṇī Saṃhitā, iii. 4, 10; Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, xviii. 12.
Śatapatha brāhmaṇa, v. 1, 4, 14; 3, 3, 5; taittirīya brāhmaṇa, i. 3, 6, 7, etc.
Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 240.

Nīvi is the name of the ‘undergarment,’ probably a simple apron of cloth, worn by both men and women, but especially by the latter. It is mentioned in the Atharvaveda and later.
Foot notes viii. 2, 16; xiv. 2, 50. Cf. nīvibhārya, ‘to be borne in the apron,’ viii. 6, 20.
taittirīya Saṃhitā, vi. 1, 1, 3; Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, iv. 10; Satapatha brāhmaṇa, i. 3, 3, 6; iii. 2, 1, 15, etc.
Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 262; Schrader, Prehistoric Antiquities, 331.
